Court No. - 70  HON'BLE SANTOSH RAI, J. 
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant; Sri Ram Sajiwan Prajapati, learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.
2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant Shivanand with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.05 of 2025, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504 and 506 IPC, Police Station Parasrampur, District Basti, during pendency of trial.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that as per the first information report, the incident is said to be occurred between 02.09.2023 and 16.11.2023 whereas F.I.R. has been registered on 08.01.2025.
No plausible explanation for lodging delay F.I.R. has been given by the prosecution.
During course of argument learned counsel for the applicant admits the fact that two sale deeds are said to be executed of the same disputed land.
First sale deed has been executed as imposter in the name of Ghirau in favour of Bablu on 02.09.2023.
Thereafter second sale deed of the same disputed land was executed by Bablu in favour of Smt. Suman on 16.11.2023.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the applicant is not vendee or vendor of the so called sale deeds.
He is only marginal witness of the first sale deed.
He is not beneficiary in this case.
He has no criminal history to his credit and is languishing in jail since 25.09.2025.
It is submitted that charge-sheet has already been submitted, therefore, there is no reasonable possibility of intimidating or pressurizing the prosecution witnesses.

It is further argued that the conclusion of trial will take sufficiently long and there is no likelihood of accused applicant fleeing from course of justice or tampering with evidence in case of release on bail.
Hence, bail has been prayed for.

4.
Learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed bail prayer of the applicant and submitted that accused-applicant is relative of co-accused Sandeep Kumar.
Sale-deed was executed in the name of Sandeep Kumar in the first sale deed.
When the fact of committing forgery was known to the informant, the informant filed civil suit before the competent which has been withdrawn by the informant due to some formal defect.
Thereafter fresh civil suit has been filed before the competent court against Sandeep Kumar and Bablu which is pending.
They further contended that the innocence of the applicant cannot be adjudged at pre trial stage, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence.
In case the applicant is released on bail he will again indulge in similar activities and will misuse the liberty of bail.

5. Having considered the submissions of the parties noted above, finding force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant; period of detention in jail, keeping in view uncertainty regarding conclusion of trial; larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India, bail application is allowed.

6. Considering the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Shivanand vs State Of U.P. on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106149025/
2 Enforcement, 2024 LawSuit (SC) 677, considering 5-6 times overcrowding in jails over and above their capacity by under trials and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, let the applicant involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions that :-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or as directed by the Court.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A I.P.C./269 B.N.S.
(iv) In case the applicant misuse the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C./84 B.N.S.S. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation then the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law under Section 174-A I.P.C./209. B.N.S.
(v) The applicant shall remain present in person before the Trial Court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
7. In case, of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
8. Identity and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
(Santosh Rai,J.) November 6, 2025
